full_judgment:
AKM Abdul Hakim J: In this writ petition, the petitioner called in question the legality of the order No. 101 dated 17-7-2006 passed by the learned Judge of the Artha Rin Adalat No. 1, Dhaka in Execution Case No. 88 of 1989 rejecting the application for setting aside the auction sale of the petitioners property held on 14-9-2003 without realising the decretal amount from the properties of the principal debtor/ loanee, respondent No. 5. 

 2. Facts necessary for disposal of the Rule, in brief, are as follows: Respondent No. 2 Sonali Bank, Principal Office, Dhaka (hereinafter referred to as the Bank), as plaintiff, instituted Title Suit No. 217 of 1987 in the Court of Subordinate Judge and Commercial Court No. 1, Dhaka impleading the petitioner and others as defendants of this suit for realisation of Taka 1,35,772 only. The suit was decreed against the defendants on 28-2-1989 in preliminary form and preliminary decree was drawn and signed on 22-6-1989. The suit was finally decreed on 22-6-1989. The petitioner as appellant preferred First Appeal No. 34 of 1990 and the same was dismissed with cost on 19-5-1994. Being aggrieved by the judgment passed by the High Court Division the petitioner filed Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 343 of 1994 which was dismissed on 7-5-1995. The defendant having failed to pay the decretal amount, the Bank on 16-10-1989 filed Execution Case No. 88 of 1989 for realisation of decretal amount. Respondent No. 3 i.e. decree holder Bank published auction sale notice in daily Ittefaq on 4-9-2003 to sell out the mortgaged properties of the judgment-debtors and the auction date was fixed on 14-9-2003 and on that date the property was auction sold and same was purchased by the auction purchaser i.e. respondent Nos. 6 and 7. Petitioner filed an application on 12-7-2006 under section 6(5) read with section 57 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 praying for setting aside the auction sale and further proceeding of Execution Case. But the Adalat by the impugned order No. 101 dated 17-7-2006 rejected the said application. Hence, this writ petition. 

 3. Petitioner filed supplementary-affidavit on 18-3-2009 stating that the principal loanee took loan for an amount of Taka 1,50,000. The petitioner on misconception filed Miscellaneous Case No. 33 of 2005 in the Court of District Judge, Dhaka by paying half portion of decretal amount i.e. Taka 71,436 and earlier on different occasions the petitioner also deposited Taka 55,000 to the respondent-Bank. 

 4. Respondent No. 3 Sonali Bank contested the Rule by filing affidavit-in-opposition and a supplementary-affidavit-in-opposition dated 3-2-2009 contending, inter alia, that the learned Judge of the Artha Rin Adalat passed the impugned order dated 17-7-2006 in Execution Case No. 88 of 1989 after considering the facts and circumstances of this case and the relevant laws because guarantors liability is equal like loanee to pay the loan amount. The petitioner has no right to stay the said execution case against him. The respondent put the mortgaged property in auction to sell out said property as per provision of Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 (shortly, the Ain). The petitioner cannot get remedy on the plea that the judgment-debtor No. 2 is liable to pay the decretal amount and, as such, this writ petition is not maintainable. The application filed by the petitioner before the Artha Rin Adalat i.e. (Annexure-G to the writ petition) are incorrect and misleading and the present Rule has been obtained by the petitioner by suppressing the actual position and he did not come with clean hands. So he is not entitled to get any relief in this writ petition. Therefore, the Rule is liable to be discharged with cost. 

 5. Respondent Nos. 6 and 7 also contested the Rule by filing affidavit-in-opposition contending, inter alia, that the petitioner has not annexed the judgment of the Appellate Division and the order of Civil Revision; that the auction sale was held legally in compliance with the prescribed legal procedure and observing all the legal requirements and formalities; that the auction purchaser deposited the entire bid money within the time prescribed in law; that from the auction notice (Annexure-E to the writ petition) it is apparent that both scheduled properties were put into auction, but only schedule-1 property was sold in auction; that in this writ petition the petitioner raised certain disputed question of facts which is not amenable in the writ jurisdiction; that Miscellaneous Case No. 33 and Miscellaneous Appeal No. 207 of 2005 were rightly rejected on the ground of limitation in accordance with law. The writ petition is misconceived, incorrect and merits no consideration and, as such, the Rule is liable to be discharged with cost. 

 9. The moot question to be decided in the Rule is, whether impugned order dated 17-7-2006 passed by the learned Judge of the Artha Rin Adalat in Execution Case No. 88 of 1989 rejecting the petitioner's application under section 6(5) read with section 57 of the Ain is lawful. 

 11. It appears from the writ petition that the Bank filed Title Suit No. 217 of 1987 impleading the petitioners and others as defendant of the suit. The principal loanee i.e. defendant No. 1, appeared and contested the suit and petitioner-defendant Nos. 2 and 3' party mortgagor also filed a separate written statement admitting taking of loan by defendant No. 1 and he mortgaged his property as security to the loan. It further appears that the suit was decreed on 21-8-1989 and the petitioner preferred First Appeal No. 34 of 1990 and the same was dismissed with costs on 9-5-1994 by a Division Bench of High Court Division and the petitioner also preferred Leave to Appeal No. 343 of 1994 which was also dismissed of 7-5-1995. Therefore, it is clear from the writ petition itself that the petitioner fought upto Appellate Division to set aside the decree but failed. Thereafter, judgment-debtors having failed to pay the decretal amount, the Bank filed Execution case for auction sale of the mortgaged property. It appears from the judgment and decree dated 14-2-1989 (decree signed on 28-2-1989 Annexures 1 and 2 to the Supplementary affidavit-in-opposition) filed by respondent No. 2 that only schedule 1 of the property was included in the decree which was admittedly mortgaged by the petitioner in favour of the Bank. The description of the property included in the decree does not contain schedule 2 property. There was no other mortgaged property in favour of the Bank except the property of the petitioner and in the decree it has been clearly stated that:— 

 12. Therefore, according to the terms of the decree, the schedule property i.e. Schedule 1 of the execution case is to be sold for realisation of the decretal amount if the defendant-judgment-debtors fail to pay the decretal amount. Thus, there was no scope to sell any other property beyond the decree, inasmuch as the decree included only the mortgaged property. If after sale of the mortgaged property the decree is not satisfied then other properties of the judgment-debtors may be attached and sold to satisfy the decree. 

 15. In our considered view, this provision is applicable only when the properties were mortgaged both by the principal debtor /loanee and the third party mortgagor. In the instant case, admittedly no property was mortgaged by the principal debtor loanee but the property was mortgaged by the petitioner. So, in absence of any other property mortgaged by the principal debtor in favour of the Bank, the mortgaged property of the petitioner-judgment-debtor is to be sold to realise the decretal amount. Therefore, the Adalat was bound to sell the mortgaged property which was included in the schedule of the plaint/decree." 

 17. Therefore, we find no illegality in the impugned order passed by the learned Judge of the Artha Rin Adalat. Rather, the impugned order is found to be well founded in law in the given facts and circumstances of the case.
